column3: BSB follows the critical text with “loved” (the Textus Receptus has “sanctified”). “By God the Father” renders “in God [the] Father.”
BSB leaves out the second “and” between “peace” and “love.”
“Although I made every effort” renders “using all diligence”; “the salvation we share” renders “our common salvation”; “entrusted” renders παραδοθείσῃ (“delivered”).
BSB follows the critical text with “our only Master and Lord” (no “God”). It adds “among you” and “for” in “for condemnation”; “a license for immorality” renders ἀσέλγειαν (“sensuality”).
BSB has “Jesus,” as in the current critical text (manuscripts vary); the Textus Receptus has “the Lord.” “You are fully aware of this” renders “knowing all things”; “His” before “people” is added.
“Bound for judgment on that great day” renders “unto [the] judgment of [the] great day.”
“Are on display as an example of those who sustain the punishment” recasts “are set forth as an example, undergoing the penalty.” BSB leaves out “in like manner to these.”
“Their bodies” renders “[the] flesh.”
BSB adds “even”; “did not presume” renders “did not dare.”
BSB renders “they corrupt themselves” as “they will be destroyed.”
“Rushed headlong” adds “headlong”; BSB leaves out “for reward” (μισθοῦ).
“Shamelessly” renders ἀφόβως (“fearlessly”); BSB adds “only” and joins “twice dead after being uprooted.”
“Blackest darkness” renders “the gloom of darkness.”
“Is coming” renders ἦλθεν (“has come”); BSB leaves out “saying.”

BSB follows the Textus Receptus here with “to convict all the ungodly”; the critical text has πᾶσαν ψυχὴν (“every soul”). “Every ungodly act of wickedness” compresses “all their works of ungodliness which they have done ungodly.”
“Spew arrogance” renders “speaks great swelling [words]”; “flatter others for their own advantage” renders “admiring faces for the sake of profit.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB puts the apostles’ words in quotation marks as direct speech.
“Devoid of the Spirit” renders “not having [the] Spirit.”
Close to the Greek.
“To bring you eternal life” renders “unto eternal life.”
BSB follows the critical text with “those who doubt” (the Textus Receptus has “making a distinction”).
BSB follows the critical text with three groups (“and to still others show mercy”); the Textus Receptus has two. “Tempered with fear” renders “with fear.”
“In His glorious presence” renders “in the presence of His glory”; “great joy” renders “exultation.”
BSB follows the critical text: no “wise,” and it includes “through Jesus Christ our Lord” and “before all time.”
